newsitem.title: USA: SEC APPROVES NASD'S NEW DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES.
newsitem.headline: SEC APPROVES NASD'S NEW DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers said Thursday the Securities and Exchange Commission has approved its new procedures for disciplining securities industry professionals.
Improvements to the NASD's disciplinary process were called for as part of a settlement reached earlier with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Under the new procedures, professional hearing officers will be added to the process, among other changes. The new hearing officers will conduct all disciplinary hearings, draft decisions and lead the special panels.

"Adding professional hearing officers to the mix of decision makers ensures that all of our disciplinary hearings will run efficiently and protect investors by applying our rules evenly," said Frank Zarb, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and President of NASD.

The Office of Hearing Officers, staffed by seven officers and a chief and deputy chief hearing officer, will begin hearing cases immediately, the NASD said. Each hearing panel will be comprised of a hearing officer and two other members.
The NASD said the SEC has also approved its rules governing how new members are admitted to the organization.
